deadline_report.summary: A-control: 292 of 799 cycles missed the 10 ms deadline (36.5%); worst response 41.0 ms, 99th percentile 38.4 ms, mean 10.40 ms. The misses form 75 run(s) of consecutive misses (longest 5); what started each run: waiting for a lock (72), late wake-up (scheduling latency) (3).

result.summary: 1 finding(s); most likely: Priority inversion on a mutex in rtdemo[2924565] (high confidence).

findings.title: Priority inversion on a mutex in rtdemo[2924565]
findings.explanation: rtdemo[2924565] 'A-control' (priority 30) waits for a mutex held by rtdemo[2924565] 'C-logger' (priority 10), while rtdemo[2924565] 'B-worker' (priority 20) keeps the CPU. The holder cannot finish its critical section until the middle-priority work stops, so the high-priority thread waits for unrelated work.
evidence: In 7 of 20 snapshots rtdemo[2924565] 'A-control' (priority 30) was blocked on the mutex at 0x288b8de060, for up to 22 ms.

The mutex holder was rtdemo[2924565] 'C-logger' at priority 10 (read from the mutex's owner word in process memory) in 7 of those snapshots: below the waiter, so it was not running at the waiter's priority.
In 7 snapshot(s) a thread between the two priorities had the holder's CPU: rtdemo[2924565] 'B-worker' at priority 20 (RUNNING).
The mutex's protocol flags say PTHREAD_PRIO_NONE (from its count word, flag _NTO_SYNC_PRIONONE)
The deadline report for A-control shows 292 misses in 75 run(s) of consecutive misses; 72 of those runs started with a long lock wait (worst lock wait 37.8 ms).
could_not_determine: Snapshots are instants: 20 were taken. They show these states happened, not how often or for how long overall.
The holder is decoded from the mutex's owner word using a layout observed on QNX 8.0 (pid low bits and tid); it is not a documented interface. The pid bits matched in 7 of 7 reads.
Which source line created or locks this mutex: the rule sees addresses and threads, not code.
Whether other locks or resources also delay the waiter.
A worst case: finite runs cannot prove the deadline will always be met after a fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the mutex use priority inheritance, the QNX default: create it with PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT (or without setting a protocol) instead of PTHREAD_PRIO_NONE. The holder then runs at the waiter's priority while the waiter is blocked, so a middle-priority thread can no longer delay it.
